title: connector-imap + minimal service-mailbox: shared-mailbox (forward/BCC) ingest into `sys_mail_message`, associated at ingest through the seam — phase 1 of #8998 inbound mail
body:
Filing gate: ④ — a per-layer child of the coordination node #8998. Part of #8998.

Blocked-by: #22870

Provenance: same as #22870.
- Design record #8998 `5311578770`, maintainer verbatim 「同意，请记录你的分析结论，但是这个任务我刻意标了 v18，暂时不做。」
- Phase-1 carve ordered in `6038989766`.
- Filed on the maintainer's order in session `session_01EgxC4UNYnzhuvmG12fh5A8`, verbatim 「该关的关，改开卡的开卡」.

This card carries phase 1's **ingest half**. It waits on #22870, which publishes the object (`sys_mail_message`) and the association seam this card writes to and calls.

## Scope

Taken from the design record. ⛔ Nothing here re-decides it.

- **`packages/connectors/connector-imap`**: protocol and auth only, following the existing connector convention (`connector-rest`, `connector-openapi`, `connector-mcp`, `connector-slack`). The account + credential abstraction is shaped for the per-user mailbox now. The shared mailbox is its first implementor (decision 4), so per-user sync later extends it rather than rewriting it.
- **`packages/services/service-mailbox`, minimal**:
  - folder cursor and UID state;
  - incremental fetch, dedupe and threading;
  - attachment extraction;
  - bounce and auto-reply suppression.

  It writes `sys_mail_message`, calls the seam at ingest and stamps the association. Unmatched messages go to the pool, and the explicit re-match action retro-matches them (decisions 2 and 3).
- Phase-1 privacy semantic: "forwarding is consent" (decision 5).
- ⛔ Out of scope, as chained follow-ups filed once phase 1 proves out:
  - per-user IMAP sync;
  - CalDAV and calendar;
  - write-back;
  - the enterprise admin plane (tenant-wide delegation, bulk provisioning, sync health).

**Why one card covers two packages:** phase 1's connector has exactly one consumer (this service), and neither can be proven end to end alone. The lane may split it at claim time through `pm:retriage`.

## Acceptance

An end-to-end test against an in-process IMAP server double:
- A forwarded message ingested from the shared mailbox lands as **one** `sys_mail_message` row, with the association stamped by an app-supplied resolver.
- A second fetch dedupes, and the row count stays 1.
- An unmatched message lands in the pool, and the re-match action associates it once a matching record exists.
- An auto-reply is suppressed.

Each clause has a negative control that fails when the behaviour is removed.

## Who acts

The `domain:services` seat, size L, once #22870 lands. Clause-②: yes, because it adds two published packages.

## Dedup

Same queries and readings as #22870. No mail-ingest, IMAP or calendar card exists besides #8998.
